Tanker hit ~50 nm N of Qatar (4 Nov)
UKMTO: a tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nm north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, late on 4 Nov; damage and crew status unconfirmed (position approximate).

IRGC: 5 ships hit mines (4-5 Nov)
The IRGC claims four tankers hit mines south of the strait on 4 Nov and two tankers and a tug caught fire on 5 Nov; none confirmed by UKMTO, location approximate.
3
Only 5 Hormuz crossings (4 Nov)
Windward counted 5 crossings on 4 Nov (1 dark) after 3 on 3 Nov, against 84-140 a day pre-war; no tanker crossed outbound (area approximate).
4
197 ships holding in Gulf (4 Nov), up from 158
straits.live counted 197 AIS-visible ships holding in the Strait and Gulf watch box on 4 Nov, up from 158 on 3 Nov (area approximate).
5
Tanker hit 14 nm NE of Lima (3 Nov)
UKMTO: two unknown projectiles struck a tanker's engine room about 14 nm north-east of Lima, Oman at 19:00 GMT on 3 Nov; no injuries.
6
Bypass routes >40% of Gulf exports
Kpler: pipelines avoiding Hormuz carry over 40% of regional exports vs 17% pre-war; Yanbu loadings 2.21 mb/d in 1-25 Oct vs 2.54 in September.
7
Hormuz crude 10.2 mb/d in Oct (60% of pre-war)
Kpler: about 10.23 mb/d of Gulf crude crossed Hormuz in October; all Gulf crude and condensate exports were about 16.1 mb/d vs 17.09 in September.
GULF OIL FLOWS · updated 6 Nov 2026

Less oil is leaving the Gulf than before the war: Kpler counts about 16.1 mb/d of crude and condensate across Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Gulf of Oman in October (down about 1 mb/d from September), of which only about 10.2 mb/d of crude went through Hormuz itself, about 60% of the 17.1 mb/d pre-war level. Visible traffic through the strait is almost nil, with Windward counting 5 crossings on 4 Nov after 3 on 3 Nov, so the Yanbu and Fujairah bypass routes carry over 40% of exports while 197 ships wait in the Gulf. Attacks continued this week: UKMTO reports a tanker hit by two projectiles about 50 nm north of Qatar late on 4 Nov, and the IRGC claims five ships hit mines around the strait (unconfirmed). Trump said on 5 Nov he will decide 'soon' between new strikes and a deal, while Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its seven conditions are met.
